edges.notes: Alpine ships Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
Alpine uses musl as the standard C library on supported architectures per project documentation.
Alpine userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC and related toolchain packages are provided via Alpine repositories for builds.
GNU binutils are used in standard Alpine build and link flows packaged in the distro.
Clang/LLVM packages may be installed from Alpine repos for alternative compiler stacks.
Official and community OCI images commonly use Alpine as a minimal musl-based base; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
CRI/containerd nodes run Alpine-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts.
Kubernetes pods frequently use Alpine-class images on Linux nodes; not an exclusive pairing.
Alpine bases are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
